policy: No source enters training until its immutable revision, upstream rights, actual schema/splits, Spanish rows, quality, privacy, exact and near-duplicate overlap against v3.1 and the other sources have been checked.

decisions.reason: Potentially useful synthetic instruction/chat; inspect generation artifacts, repetition, answer quality and exact Spanish split.
Potentially useful multi-turn persona-conditioned dialogue; require language filtering and separate persona/dialogue deduplication.
Sector-skewed cultural/theatre profiles; not representative population data. Keep only useful non-sensitive profile/style fields.
Do not train Big Five, demographic, attachment or sensitive/psychometric conditioning. Only consider non-sensitive fictional style/preferences fields after schema review.
Psychometric trait labels add little to the desired stable model identity, overlap conceptually with StrataSynth, and risk teaching personality scores as real traits. Exclude from v3.2.
741 of 803 rows were already admitted to v3.1. Do not reimport; only use remaining 62 after exact/near dedup and content audit if worthwhile.
55 rows already admitted to v3.1. Do not reimport those rows; remaining examples require context-length and overlap audit.
Potentially valuable domain-specific Spanish instruction; require jurisdiction/date metadata, upstream rights and removal of protected test/validation splits.
Useful Spanish public-administration procedures; retain official URLs, dates and provenance; exclude stale or superseded procedures.
Do not ingest benchmark/test, human-rated evaluation subsets or generated data without separate provenance. Only clearly licensed train partition can be reconsidered.
Potentially large high-value academic Spanish corpus; verify each document's CC-BY grant, author/privacy issues, boilerplate and near-duplicate theses.
No bulk admission. Require item-level public-domain proof, OCR quality and cross-dedup against Spanish-PD-Books.
No bulk admission. Require item-level public-domain proof, edition/translation rights and cross-dedup against BDH-Books.

Exclude the bulk release: per-document rights, upstream provenance and extreme scale make blanket licensing and exhaustive audit unsafe. A separately extracted, fully traceable allowlisted subset may be proposed later.
Never flatten query/positive/negative triples into ordinary SFT. Preserve retrieval objective; exclude benchmark leakage and source text with unresolved rights.
MIT wrapper metadata is not proof of rights for Wikimedia article text. Exclude until article-level attribution, revision and compatible share-alike obligations are verified.
Potentially useful Spanish biomedical entity extraction; train split only, preserve span labels and attribution; never turn into medical advice.
Clinical-note/de-identification data has elevated re-identification and upstream-rights risk. Exclude unless source-level privacy and licensing review passes.
Potentially useful disease-mention extraction; train split only, preserve task labels and provenance; not medical dialogue.
Current registry points to an aggregator rather than a sufficiently pinned canonical source. Exclude until original source, revision and rights are independently established.
